title: AI-Native Product & Design Leader
subtitle: Design leadership that stayed hands-on — a team, a system across surfaces, and the work itself

bio.short: Design leader who still designs. Fifteen years of B2B software, five direct reports at Ninox, product management and all of product design held together at ChurchDesk.
bio.long:
Start with the team. At Ninox I ran a design function of five including a design lead, on the Senior Leadership Team. I hired two people, promoted two, and made the call when someone was not the right fit. I was interim Head of Product for four months. When a working relationship kept breaking down I changed the conditions rather than managing the person: written agendas, material sent ahead, decisions recorded, turn-taking on purpose. The contribution that had been getting routed around became some of the team's strongest.

At ChurchDesk I held product management for the platform and all of its design at once. I wrote the specs and ran the ticket board two engineers worked from. A funeral-booking project was already funded and scoped when I arrived, and the internal plan was a standalone add-on module. I built the booking capability into the platform instead. Coordination time fell 70%, bookings ran at 90% acceptance, and it shipped to the whole customer base for room rentals and weddings as much as funerals.

Design systems are where I am most useful across surfaces. At Bibel TV the system ships as an API: DTCG tokens in three tiers, built with Style Dictionary, synced live to Figma and Android with iOS and web ready, so one commit propagates everywhere and consistency holds structurally instead of by coordination. Alongside it I built the colour engine — a colour-extraction API and config tool, live in production, deriving card gradients perceptually from content artwork and holding WCAG contrast in light and dark. That is brand as a system rather than brand as a drawing: the machinery that makes a visual language hold across content nobody has seen yet.

I prototype in real code against real production APIs, web first then Android. Engineering consumes that code directly and around 70% of it reaches production with minor modification; iteration moved from days to hours. Engineering there is an external agency, so that handoff crosses a company boundary and holds anyway. I direct the model rather than typing the framework, and I would rather say so than have you find it later.

Most of my customers never chose to be software users — funeral directors, parish assistants, priests, analysts inside banks and insurers. That is the same shape as tradespeople, doctors and law firms.

context.emphasis: Leadership scope that stayed hands-on, design systems across product, web and brand, brand as a system rather than art direction, AI-first practice, and customers who are not software people.
